name: Grype
evidence: Official README describes a vulnerability scanner installed on the operator machine and demonstrates local image, directory and SBOM scans. Its scanning interface is a CLI, not a shared hosted scan endpoint.

name: Atom
evidence: Official README describes an Electron text editor and distributes Windows, Linux and macOS installers. Its editor API requires the installed application rather than offering a hosted HTTPS service.

name: Brackets
evidence: Official README identifies Brackets as a code editor for HTML and CSS. The indexed application is editor software rather than a hosted public data API.

name: Mark Text
evidence: Official README identifies an open-source Markdown editor and supplies architecture-specific desktop installers. Its application interface requires installed software.

name: Lapce
evidence: Official README distributes pre-built releases for Windows, Linux and macOS or package-manager installation. This indexed code editor is desktop software rather than a hosted public HTTP API.

name: Obsidian
evidence: Official API repository documents plugin classes inside the Obsidian application, including App, Vault and Workspace and importing Node or Electron modules. This is an in-application plugin API, not a shared HTTPS service.

name: Dendron
evidence: Official README describes a local-first Markdown note-taking tool integrated with VS Code and VSCodium. The indexed interface needs that application environment, not a shared public HTTP endpoint.

name: Logseq
evidence: Official README directs users to install the application on their device and documents desktop and mobile applications. Its application/plugin interface is not a shared hosted data API.

name: Zettlr
evidence: Official README distributes desktop installers and describes Zettlr as an Electron-based application. This application interface requires a running installation.

name: Kube-bench
evidence: Official README identifies a tool that runs CIS Kubernetes checks against a Kubernetes deployment. The indexed scanner must run in an operator environment rather than providing a shared public HTTP service.

name: Cosign
evidence: Official README installs a command-line signing and verification program and demonstrates local command execution. This tool interface is not itself a hosted HTTPS data service; separate Sigstore infrastructure is not the indexed CLI.

name: Falco
evidence: Official README describes a Linux runtime security tool and kernel monitoring agent observing syscalls. The indexed software must run on a monitored system rather than exposing a shared hosted data API.

name: Mirage JS
evidence: Official README identifies Mirage as a client-side server for developing, testing and prototyping JavaScript applications. The simulated API runs in the application environment, not on a shared hosted service.

name: Vercel AI SDK
evidence: Official package README identifies a provider-agnostic TypeScript toolkit installed with npm on Node.js. This SDK entry is application software; Vercel AI Gateway is a distinct hosted service requiring separate access.

name: Llama.cpp
evidence: Official README instructs users to install llama.cpp on their machine and describes inference on local or cloud hardware. Its inference server requires an operator deployment rather than providing a shared keyless endpoint.

name: Promptflow
evidence: Official README describes development tools, local Python package installation and deploying developed flows to production. Its software interface requires a configured runtime rather than a shared public data endpoint.

name: PostgREST
evidence: Official README serves an API from an existing PostgreSQL database and instructs operators to install PostgREST or Docker. A database and operator deployment are required; the project itself is not a shared public data endpoint.

name: Shepherd.js
evidence: Official README distinguishes the standalone JavaScript library, embedded into an application or website for guided tours, from commercial services. The indexed Shepherd.js library is not a hosted data API.

name: Zetta
evidence: Official README describes a Node.js IoT platform and quick start that installs software, creates a project and starts a Zetta server. This requires a deployment rather than supplying a shared public instance.

name: Zetta IoT
evidence: Official README describes a Node.js IoT platform and quick start that installs software, creates a project and starts a Zetta server. This requires a deployment rather than supplying a shared public instance.

name: CapRover
evidence: Official README describes a deployment and web-server manager for applications and databases on the operator server. The project requires operator infrastructure rather than supplying a shared public data API.

name: Atlantis
evidence: Official README explicitly describes a self-hosted Go application listening for Terraform pull-request webhook events. It requires an operator installation and is not a shared public data service.

name: Fixer
evidence: Official provider README states that the replacement Fixer endpoint requires an access_key query parameter and that legacy users must register for an API access key. It is not eligible for credential-free execution.

name: Weatherstack
evidence: Official getting-started documentation authenticates requests using the account API access key in the access_key parameter. An account credential is required, so this is not a keyless public rail.

name: OPC UA
evidence: Official OPC Foundation architecture describes an interoperability framework implemented by clients and servers across embedded devices and cloud infrastructure. This indexed standard requires an implementation and server address; it is not itself a hosted HTTPS data endpoint.

name: XMPP
evidence: Official XMPP overview defines an XML messaging and presence protocol with decentralized client and server implementations. The indexed protocol is not a shared HTTP GET data API; participating messaging servers are separate services.

name: LoRaWAN
evidence: Official LoRa Alliance overview defines a network protocol and architecture consisting of end devices, radio gateways, network servers and application servers. The indexed communications standard is not a hosted HTTPS data endpoint.

name: Zigbee
evidence: Official Connectivity Standards Alliance documentation defines a low-power wireless mesh standard for smart devices and describes physical radio bands, device certification and interoperability. This indexed communications standard is not a shared HTTPS data service.
